name: JumpFarm staking rebase catches up one stale epoch per stake or unstake
summary: JumpFarm's Olympus-fork Staking.stake() and unstake(_rebase=true) call rebase(), which advances only one epoch per call and pays that epoch's distributor-minted reward to current sJUMP holders, with no warmup. The epoch clock was about 60 epochs behind, so the attacker bought JUMP with 15 flash-loaned WETH, cycled stake/unstake to collect the backlog of rebases on the whole position and sold the inflated JUMP back into the JUMP/WETH pair; two blocks later it repeated this on the FUMOG fork of the same staking template.
notes: Reset is setDistributor (staking slot 5), which installed the distributor whose treasury mints fund each epoch's reward; the staking contract was deployed 2,420 blocks earlier. The seed's fee-on-transfer explanation is wrong: the trace shows each stake/unstake call running sJUMP.rebase and distributor.distribute once.

The campaign transaction hit QWAStaking 0x69422c7f (FUMOG, another deployer's copy of the same Olympus staking code, idle since block 17942165). Loss is the WETH that left the JUMP/WETH pair 0x20746fde (2.7233) and the FUMOG/WETH pair 0xdb98950d (0.9626); the inflated tokens the pairs received are not counted (rule 12). 0.31 WETH of the JUMP pair's outflow went to JumpFarm's own tax wallets.
